changes: Updated Lattice-lifecycle-memory-Evolving.md with a 100-point MemoryScore baseline, including HistoricalRetrievalScore, exact recall@1, recall@10, MRR@10, precision@10, ExactAnswerHit, EvidenceLinkageRate, LayerRoutingAccuracy, ScaleStabilityScore, 10k/100k/1M thresholds, boundary-only layer labels, and staleTruthHit taxonomy.
usage: Use the MemoryScore section as the future benchmark contract when implementing lifecycle memory recall: hard checks run first, then score retrieval, exact answers, evidence linkage, layer routing, and scale stability without treating the score as authority.
expectedOutcome: User can read the document and see exactly how memory ability is scored, including screenshot retrieval metrics and 10k/100k/1M thresholds.
actualTranscript: The document now shows HistoricalRetrievalScore = (exact recall@1 + recall@10 + MRR@10 + precision@10) / 4, Expanded MemoryScore = 25 * HistoricalRetrievalScore + 25 * ExactAnswerHit + 25 * EvidenceLinkageRate + 15 * LayerRoutingAccuracy + 10 * ScaleStabilityScore, score thresholds for 10,000 / 100,000 / 1,000,000 candidates, boundary-only labels for advisory and host transcript memory, and the statement that MemoryScore is not lifecycle truth, review pass, validation evidence, delivery check, receipt, or production authority. koala validate passed with 6/6 verification coverage.
outcomeDiff: No user-value gap: the requested scoring baseline and screenshot metrics are included, and reviewer findings about layer boundaries, expanded formula, staleTruthHit taxonomy, and evidence coverage were resolved.
limitations: No benchmark harness, storage backend, vector DB, embedding model, external provider, or actual million-candidate run was implemented; this story only documents the future validation contract.
pitfalls: Avoided recursive scale scoring by using QualityScoreAtScale instead of MemoryScoreAtScale, and clarified boundary-only memory labels so excluded sources do not enter corpus/gold/recall/precision.
